happens to a row across runs. Each case is a REPLAY - the same record seen
two or three times, with what the table must say afterwards. This is where
'repeat import creates no duplicates' and 'handle edits and removals' are

cases.why: The plainest version of the M2 check: seeing a record again updates when we last saw it and nothing else.

cases.why: The author edits, then the text sits still. One revision, dated when we first noticed - not one per sighting.

cases.why: The source stops returning it. The row survives - the signal was real when it was collected, and an archive that silently loses rows cannot reconcile its own counts.
